speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your recent trip to Miami and the intense itching with red bumps on your thigh, have you noticed any mosquito bites, or perhaps been in an area with tall grass or new plants? Additionally, are these bumps accompanied by any pain, warmth, or swelling, and have you taken any specific medications or lotions since the symptoms started?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).
REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up photograph of the rash lesions on the thigh.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC): WBC 7,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CBC and ESR suggest an allergic or parasitic etiology rather than a severe bacterial infection. Based on your recent trip to Miami and the description of intense itching with red bumps, did the lesions appear in a linear or clustered pattern, and do you recall seeing or touching any specific plants or insects? Also, have you noticed any hives or swelling elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Doctor

REQUEST TEST: Peripheral Blood Eosinophil Count.
REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up photograph of the rash lesions on the thigh.
Based on the travel history and medication list, could you confirm if the bumps are strictly on areas exposed to clothing or if they are in hidden areas, and do you have a history of scabies or eczema?

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal eosinophil count makes a systemic parasitic infection like strongyloidiasis less likely. Given your recent trip to Miami and the location of the bumps, were you sleeping outdoors or did you notice any small mites on your bedding or clothing? Also, is the itching so severe that it causes you to scratch until your skin breaks or bleeds?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you denied any exposure to mites or sleeping outdoors, and considering your recent trip to Miami, did you notice if the itching is worse at night or if the bumps appear in a line or cluster suggestive of bed bugs or chiggers? Also, have you tried any over-the-counter hydrocortisone or antihistamines to see if the itching subsided?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Papular Urticaria (likely from mosquito or insect bites during recent travel to Miami).
